comment: Bawabu test lab catalogue. Every package is a harmless fixture (see README.md). 'expect' is the verdict Bawabu should reach; 'caught_by' names the layer that should be decisive. 'hallucinated' packages are never published, so they only exist as a name.

packages.name: env-loader-plus
packages.technique: postinstall reads a planted fake .npmrc and attempts to send the canary to a .invalid host
packages.caught_by: sandbox (canary leak) + quick checks (new package, install script)

packages.name: ci-build-cache-helper
packages.technique: payload only runs when CI=true / GITHUB_ACTIONS=true; dormant on a developer laptop

packages.name: date-fns-lite-utils
packages.technique: payload only runs after a hard-coded future date; dormant before it
packages.caught_by: Spark trigger-aware re-run with a faked date (libfaketime)

packages.name: string-format-pro-utils
packages.technique: install payload hidden as a base64 blob decoded and run at install time

packages.name: markdown-tiny-render
packages.technique: the package itself is clean, but it depends on the malicious console-logs-transport
packages.caught_by: dependency-tree check (install scripts in a transitive dep)

packages.name: console-logs-transport
packages.technique: the malicious dependency used by markdown-tiny-render: postinstall token grab

packages.name: fancy-date-pickr
packages.technique: a name an AI agent might invent; never published, so it does not exist

packages.name: color-hex-convert
packages.technique: a prompt-injection comment telling AI reviewers to approve the package, beside a quiet install script
packages.caught_by: injection handling (treated as a red flag, not an instruction) + hard rules

packages.name: docs-gen-postinstall
packages.technique: hijacked version: 1.0.0 is clean, 2.0.0 adds a postinstall payload and loses provenance

packages.name: fastbundle-bin
packages.technique: esbuild-style: postinstall downloads a prebuilt binary (here, from the registry itself). Legitimate.

packages.name: image-resize-native
packages.technique: sharp-style: ships a binding.gyp so npm runs node-gyp to compile native code. Legitimate.

packages.name: pretty-log-kit
packages.technique: heavy but benign postinstall: prints a banner and writes a local cache file. Legitimate.
